speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether he can provide a status update on the Single Room Shared Facilities initiative; and (b) what suggestions are received to enhance the said initiative.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With the SRSF, we aim to provide more privacy for tenants while making good use of limited space, and the shared facilities and communal spaces will enable social interaction and reduce the risk of social isolation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since the announcement, we have received feedback of interest in applying for the pilot.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also received suggestions about the amenities to be provided for the shared facilities, such as the kitchens and laundry rooms; received suggestions on the measures that we could take to tackle social isolation; received suggestions on the manner of facilities, management and upkeep; suggestions on the types of social interventions and community services that may be provided, and we will adopt these where possible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As this is a pilot, we will work alongside the appointed social service agency operator to refine the model as we gain experience.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also wish to compliment HDB and the Ministry of National Development (MND) for this SRSF initiative, which I thought was very important because it addresses the gaps for the homeless and also the tenants who cannot get along well with each other.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, if designed well, it will reduce many of the appeals that we are receiving at our Meet-the-People sessions each week.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is because every week, we are still receiving a lot of feedback on rental tenants who just cannot get along with each other.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And the need for just more privacy for rental tenants of HDB flats is still there; the demand is there.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister about the scalability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The various suggestions came to us first in the course of our consultation before we launched the pilot in March of this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Before we launched the pilot, we had, last year, engaged social work professionals, social service agencies, academics, researchers, community workers and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of these ideas have actually been incorporated in this pilot and you will see some of these in place when we launch the first round of applications for tenants in December of this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The other ideas will be studied and some of these ideas include the kinds of social interventions that can take place for the residents of this pilot project.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When the social service agency comes on board, we will work with the operator to see whether some of these can be trialed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Let us assess how the tenants interact with each other, with the social service agency operator in the shared facilities, and let us learn from this pilot.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said that, I think it is important to contextualise this pilot, given the other things that we are doing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, we have been putting partitions in rental flats – both retrofitting existing ones as well as building new rental flats that come with partitions for individuals under the Joint Singles Scheme (JSS).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have been piloting the JSS Operator-Run pilot (JSS-OR).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we have earlier announced this year that we will extend the pilot to more sites.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This involves two individuals sharing under the JSS rental flat with a social service agency coming in to match tenants, to address disputes and, of course, to provide social support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This SRSF pilot tests the viability of giving each individual privacy in a room of his or her own.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But to prevent and tackle the risk of social isolation, you have facilities that are shared on every floor as well as on the ground floor and a social service agency with professionals coming in to provide programming, community interventions as well as social work interventions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Let it run for some time and if it is feasible, it may go into the design of future rental flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I welcome Members of this House to refer residents whom you think will benefit from this pilot.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I ask this because we do see in our rental blocks in every constituency that there is very little sense of ownership amongst the residents and pervasive littering acts, and just higher rates of dirtiness and all that happens in every single Town Council, I believe.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We know from observing human behaviour that it is easier to upkeep a place that is nice and beautiful than to transform, at your own effort, a place that is dirty into a clean place.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: My point here is, are we looking into the mechanics of what it means to enable people to live a good life so that they are more enabled in their spirit towards overcoming the circumstances that they are facing in their lives?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am responding to the controversy around, in social media when the design of the —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Perhaps, Ms Carrie Tan, you can ask your clarification?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: So, my clarification is – was there any conversation or discussion around this topic during the public consultations?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: And will MND be looking into the research around this to look at the role of aesthetics in uplifting people's spirits towards breaking out of their difficult circumstances?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of course, we had separate engagements in the lead-up to this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of these would be taken on board, as I said in the response to Member Denise Phua's query.
